priorStories.headline: FAA lifts nationwide ground stop after disruption
priorStories.body:
The FAA allowed departures to resume at 8:15 p.m. Eastern Friday, lifting a nationwide ground stop that had lasted more than four hours. Flight schedules remained disrupted afterward.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said radar data and communications had become unstable across air traffic facilities, though the agency had not lost all telecommunications. Officials attributed the disruption to overloaded older equipment, with the underlying cause still under investigation.

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said investigators had found no evidence of a cyberattack and no connection to the Microsoft outage.

candidates.summary: The Associated Press called Alaska’s governor election for Democrat Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins at 12:01 a.m. Eastern on November 14. The former state lawmaker defeated Republicans Dave Bronson, Treg Taylor and Bernadette Wilson. He will succeed term-limited Republican Governor Mike Dunleavy; the call does not constitute certification of the election.
candidates.title: AP calls Alaska governor’s race for Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins

candidates.summary: More than 2,500 U.S. flights scheduled for Saturday were canceled and hundreds more delayed, according to FlightAware figures reported by the Associated Press. The cancellations followed Friday evening’s lifting of the nationwide FAA ground stop and represent continuing disruption rather than a new nationwide flight suspension.
candidates.title: Saturday flight cancellations exceed 2,500 after FAA ground stop

candidates.summary: Microsoft said Saturday that it had addressed the underlying issue behind its global outage and restored service to the remaining affected customers and regions. The disruption affected Outlook, Teams and other products for more than 24 hours. Microsoft attributed the incident to technical problems associated with a network capacity upgrade and said it was not aware of malicious activity.
candidates.title: Microsoft announces full service recovery after global outage

candidates.summary: ASEAN foreign ministers met in Manila on November 14 under Philippine Foreign Secretary Theresa Lazaro’s chairmanship. ASEAN’s Secretariat said the meeting addressed preparations for the 49th ASEAN Summit, regional and international issues, external relations and community-building. The meeting itself did not establish adoption of the draft summit communiques or completion of a South China Sea code of conduct.
candidates.title: ASEAN foreign ministers hold pre-summit meeting in Manila

candidates.summary: More than 2,500 U.S. flights scheduled for November 14 were canceled, according to FlightAware figures reported by AP, as airlines recovered from Friday’s nationwide FAA ground stop. At a Saturday morning news conference, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said a contractor’s work replacing copper wiring with fiber had caused a system overload. He said investigators were examining whether faulty wiring or contractor performance was responsible. The cancellations were continuing disruption, not a new nationwide flight suspension.
candidates.title: Duffy links FAA disruption to wiring upgrade as Saturday cancellations continue

candidates.summary: An Israeli drone strike killed two Palestinians in Jabaliya on November 14, according to Shifa Hospital director Mohamed Abu Selmiya. The American field hospital reported additional wounded people without specifying a number. The Israeli military said it had struck two Hamas militants in the area.
candidates.title: Hospital officials report two Palestinians killed in Israeli strike in Jabaliya

candidates.summary: The Associated Press called the defeat of Alaska’s election-system repeal measure overnight on November 14, NPR reported. The measure would have repealed the state’s nonpartisan top-four primaries and ranked-choice general elections. The call concerns ballots cast in the November 3 election; it is not election certification.
candidates.title: AP calls defeat of Alaska measure to repeal ranked-choice voting

candidates.summary: SpaceX’s Starship upper stage returned from orbit on November 14 and was caught by the launch tower’s mechanical arms at Starbase, Texas, the first successful capture of a Starship spacecraft returning from space. The spacecraft completed 14 orbits during roughly 22 hours after its November 13 launch on Flight 15. The Super Heavy booster was not recovered: its attempted return on November 13 was aborted and it exploded in the Gulf of Mexico. The upper-stage recovery therefore did not constitute recovery of both stages on this flight.
candidates.title: SpaceX catches Starship upper stage after orbital flight
candidates.geography: Starbase, Texas, United States; Earth orbit

sources.name: Associated Press via South Carolina Public Radio

candidates.summary: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said November 14 that Friday’s FAA disruption began during L3Harris work switching copper telecommunications lines to fiber at a remote facility. He said a router flooded other routers with connection attempts; investigators had not determined whether installation error or faulty equipment caused it. L3Harris said it was supporting the investigation. FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford distinguished the maintenance from the separate modernization program. Thousands of Saturday flights were canceled as airlines recovered; airspace had reopened Friday, and officials said FAA systems were fully operational.
candidates.title: Duffy identifies contractor and router problem in FAA outage investigation

candidates.summary: In remarks released by his office on November 14, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy alleged that speed restrictions on SpaceX’s military-grade Starshield terminals in Russian-occupied Ukrainian territory had hampered air defenses for five days. He said he had directed military and diplomatic officials to seek clarification and removal of the restrictions. SpaceX denied introducing new restrictions or changing its satellite operations. The reported target-day development is Zelenskyy’s statement, not independently established implementation of a new restriction that day.
candidates.title: Zelenskyy challenges alleged Starshield restrictions; SpaceX denies changes
